_README: Shared staging-inference defaults. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH:
infer_stage.py reads it when no override is passed on the command line, so
the launcher's Development run and the capture web UI's 'Analyze on
laptop' button start from identical numbers. The launcher also reads it to
seed the per-class sliders and to power their 'Reset to defaults' button.
class_conf: per-class confidence floor, applied to every raw tile detection
BEFORE the boxes are merged. '_default' covers any class not named here,
so a retrained model that adds a class still runs. Key order is the order
the launcher shows the sliders in - keep it in model-class order.
PROVENANCE OF THESE NUMBERS: measured 2026-08-05 from the population-study
batch 1 — 7,265 real detections across 3 timepoints x 3 strains x 3 doses,
read out of soft_stage_scores.csv (the per-worm class-score side output).
Two findings set these values. (1) The winning-class score distribution has
NO valley: it rises smoothly to a mode at 0.70-0.78, so there is no natural
cut point and any threshold is a judgement call, not a measurement. (2) The
old numbers were inert - at 0.30 they kept 99.7% of detections, so moving a
slider did nothing. They were also unjustified per class, and backwards: L4
had the LOWEST floor (0.25) despite having the lowest scores of any class
(median 0.585 vs 0.70 for L1/L3), while adult had the highest floor (0.35)
despite scoring high.
So: one uniform value, because nothing in the data supports differentiating
the classes, and 0.40 because it is the largest floor that is still
demonstrably safe - it trims 6.6% of detections, shifts per-plate survival
by at most 2.4 points, and moves no plate by more than 3. Above ~0.50 the
cost climbs fast (0.60 drops 29% of detections and moves one plate by 9).
THIS IS STILL NOT CALIBRATION. Low-scoring detections are size-plausible
worms, not debris, so this trims a tail rather than removing false
positives. Real calibration needs hand-labelled animals - concentrate them
in the 37-49 px band, where 50% of the population sits and where the L1/L3
survivor cutoff actually lives. Until then staging counts stay a QA readout.
L2 IS THE ONE EXCEPTION, and it is data-driven rather than a preference.
L2's score distribution is shifted far below every other class - median
0.486, against 0.717 for L1 and 0.697 for L3 - so a uniform floor is not
uniform in effect: 0.40 sits near L2's median while sitting in the tail of
every other class, i.e. it is roughly twice as strict on L2 as on anything
else. Since the per-class floor is applied to candidate boxes BEFORE the
merge, that difference decides which boxes even get to compete. L2 is held
at 0.25 so its candidates reach the merge at all.
This does NOT fix L2-being-called-L3 on its own - see the class_size_px
block below and the note there. It removes one of the two mechanisms
suppressing L2; the other is that an L2 box loses cross-class NMS to an L3
box scoring 0.7 on the same worm, which no threshold can change.
NOTE: the current model emits SIX classes (egg, L1, L2, L3, L4, adult).
There is no 'young adult'; its entry below is kept only so a retrain that
adds the class inherits a sane floor.
Per-class score rescoring. SHIPS AT ALPHA 2.0. This file is the single
source of truth for that value: Development mode's "Correct for uneven
class confidence" checkbox passes NO alpha when ticked (so this number
applies) and forces alpha 0 when unticked. Nothing in the launcher
hardcodes 2.0, so retuning is an edit here, not a rebuild.
At alpha 0 the run is bit-identical to a build without this block at all.
WHY: the class heads are not on a common scale. Measured over 17,084 real
detections (the 5-timepoint course plus the full dose experiment), the L2
head's 99th percentile is 0.14 while L1 and L3 routinely reach 0.80. Taking
an arg-max across raw scores therefore compares numbers that are not
comparable, and L2 loses every contest it enters - it won 70 times out of
17,084. That is load-bearing, because the survivor cutoff sits exactly on
the L2/L3 boundary.
THE RULE:   adjusted_c = raw_c / (ref_c ** alpha)
alpha 0   arg-max on raw scores (current behaviour, exact no-op)
alpha 1   full normalisation; moved 1.8% of calls on the measured set
0 < a < 1 a blend, e.g. 0.5
alpha > 1 OVER-normalisation, which is what ships. Read this before
changing it: the effect is EXPONENTIAL, not linear. What
decides an L2-vs-L3 contest is (ref_L3/ref_L2)**alpha, and
with the refs below that is 5.6x at alpha 1, 13.3x at 1.5
and 31.4x at 2.0. Going 1.5 -> 2.0 is a further 2.4x, not a
small step. In absolute terms alpha 2.0 multiplies L2's raw
score by ~50x and adult's by ~1.35x.
APPLIED LAST, after every suppression pass. It RELABELS ONLY: the boxes,
and the detection count, are unchanged. So a shift in survival % after
turning this on is pure reclassification, and you can prove it by checking
that the totals match.
refs are each class's measured 99th-percentile score - 'how loud does this
head ever get'. A class with no entry is left alone (reference 1.0).
'egg' is deliberately absent as well as excluded from the run: its 99th
percentile is 0.0006 and dividing by that would make egg win everything.
EVIDENCE, and its limits. At alpha 1 the newly-created L2 calls land at a
median of 43 px, between L1 (37) and L3 (50) - the size an L2 should be -
the L2/L3 size overlap falls from 0.58 to 0.53, and the fraction of L3
calls that are L2-sized drops. That is agreement with an independent
measurement, not validation.
IT IS NOT CALIBRATION. Dividing by a per-class constant implicitly assumes
the classes are equally common, and they are not: adult is ~44% of
detections and L2 ~0.4%. alpha is a lever on a prior. Validate against
hand-labelled animals before any rescored count is reported as data.
Re-measure refs after a retrain - they describe THIS checkpoint's heads.
WHY 2.0 AND NOT 1.5. David compared several alphas against his own manual
counts and found 1.5-2.0 matched best; he chose 2.0. The counter-evidence,
recorded here so it is not lost: at alpha 2 about 19% of newly-created L2
calls fall outside the plausible L2 size window (class_size_px), versus 10%
at alpha 1 and 15% at 1.5 - and the per-plate difference between 1.5 and 2.0
(mean 1.6 points) is smaller than the plate-to-plate noise in most
conditions, so that comparison probably cannot separate the two. 2.0 is a
considered choice made with this known, not a measurement that beat 1.5.

_comment: overlap only. tile_w/tile_h/imgsz are deliberately NOT settable here:
staging reads absolute worm size, so changing them silently degrades
accuracy. overlap moves where the seams fall without touching scale.
0.20 -> 56 tiles, whole-object guarantee 135x122 px
0.30 -> 63 tiles, whole-object guarantee 203x182 px
0.35 -> 72 tiles, whole-object guarantee 237x213 px (~29% slower than 0.20)
Targeted duplicate-box fix. A detection within margin_px of an INTERIOR
tile seam is flagged as a possible worm fragment, and dropped only if at
least cover_frac of its area sits inside a higher-scoring box of any
class. A fragment nothing covers is kept, so a worm is never lost.
Set cover_frac to null to disable the pass.
class_agnostic_iou: one extra NMS across ALL classes after the per-class
pass, for the case of ONE worm carrying TWO labels at nearly the same box
(the classic L3-here/L4-there pair). Per-class NMS cannot see that pair at
all - it only ever compares boxes of the same class.
At 0.70 two boxes must be almost the same rectangle to be merged, which
one object produces and two neighbouring worms realistically do not.
LOWER it (~0.55) if same-worm pairs still slip through; RAISE it if two
genuinely adjacent worms are being collapsed into one. null = off, which
is the pre-2026-07-27 behaviour.
_same_class_comment: same_class_cover_frac: drop a box sitting inside a LARGER box of the SAME
class. A big worm often yields both a whole box and a partial box at
50-70% the linear size, which puts their IoU at 0.25-0.45 - structurally
below any usable NMS threshold, so per-class NMS can never reach it.
Same-class ONLY, and that is the entire safety argument: two worms at the
same stage are the same size, so one cannot be nested inside the other.
Cross-class nesting is real biology (a gravid adult is full of eggs) and
is deliberately left alone. null = off.

_exclude_classes_README: Classes dropped from the run entirely, before any merge. Default is eggs:
a plate is almost never a question about worms AND eggs at the same time,
and egg boxes are pure clutter on a staging plate. Egg counts are wanted
for an egg-survival assay or a drop of bleached eggs — tick 'Count eggs'
in the launcher's Worm Survival card, or on the capture UI's Analyze
button, and that run keeps them.
Eggs are already excluded from the survival denominator (SURVIVAL_CONFIG
in survival.py), so this changes the egg column and the clutter, never the
An excluded class is NOT a class that scored zero. counts.txt prints
'not counted', the Excel drops the column, and run_info names the
exclusion — printing 0 would read as 'no eggs on this plate'.
Set to [] to count everything by default.

_README: Per-class plausible box size, as [min, max] of sqrt(width * height) in
full-frame pixels. Either bound may be null. A class absent from this
block is not size-gated at all.
WHY THIS EXISTS: staging is a size readout - the stages are ordered
egg < L1 < L2 < L3 < L4 < young adult < adult. A small round speck of
debris scoring 0.8 on 'adult' is not an uncertain adult, it is not a worm,
and no confidence threshold can fix that because the model is confident.
A size gate can: an adult-sized label on a debris-sized box is impossible
regardless of score.
EMPTY BY DEFAULT ON PURPOSE. The pixel size of a stage depends on the
magnification, so there is no honest default to ship - a guessed number
here deletes real worms. Measure it:
launcher\vision\.venv-vision\Scripts\python.exe ^
dev\tools\stage_conf_report.py --suggest "C:\path\to\images"
That writes stage_conf_suggested.json with a ready-to-paste block plus a
count of what each bound would have removed. Read the removal counts
before pasting.
NOTE (2026-08-18): the tool's defaults are the 2nd/98th percentile with
NO widening, while the bounds actually shipped below are the 0.5th/99.5th
widened by 15%. Re-running the command above therefore reproduces neither
the numbers nor the method. Either pass the matching percentiles or treat
the tool's output as a starting point and widen it by hand.
Boxes flagged as seam-truncated are exempt from this gate - a worm clipped
by a tile edge is legitimately undersized and is handled by the seam pass.
NOW POPULATED (2026-08-05), measured from the same 7,265 detections as
class_conf above: bounds are the 0.5th and 99.5th percentile of each
class's observed sqrt(w*h), widened by 15% on each side so they catch
gross implausibility only and never trim the real distribution.
Median size rises monotonically L1 37 -> L2 44 -> L3 49 -> L4 71 ->
adult 79 px, which is the check stage_conf_report --suggest makes before
OPEN (2026-08-18): the 'adult' lower bound of 43 px is BELOW the median
size of an L4 (71 px), i.e. roughly L1-sized, so the small debris that
scores high on 'adult' - the failure this gate was built for - still
passes it. That is the trap this block's own text warns about: the
percentiles were cut from the model's own detections, so a class already
polluted by debris has its lower bound set BY that debris. Set adult's
floor by hand instead: an adult cannot be smaller than a typical L4.
it will recommend gating a class at all: where median size does NOT rise,
the model is not separating those stages by size and must not be gated.
ON THIS DATA THE GATE REMOVES 7 DETECTIONS OUT OF 7,265 (0.1%) and moves
no plate's survival % by more than 0.03 points. That is the point: it is
not a filter for today's images, it is a guard. It costs nothing now and
catches a future regression - debris scoring high on 'adult', or a
magnification change that shifts every size - which nothing else in the
pipeline would notice. Re-measure it if the objective or the working
distance changes; these bounds are in PIXELS and are magnification-bound.
'young adult' is deliberately absent: the current model never emits it,
so there is nothing to measure and it stays ungated.
OPEN PROBLEM - L2 CALLED AS L3 (reported 2026-08-05, NOT fixed here).
30% of L3 calls (863 of 2896) sit at or below 44 px, which is the median
size of a confirmed L2 and below the 90th percentile of L1. Those are
size-implausible L3s. They are NOT low-confidence: median raw_L3 in that
band is 0.69-0.71 and median raw_L2 is 0.006, so the soft scores cannot
recover them and no confidence threshold will either. Only size can.
This is NOT gated here, deliberately, and the reason matters: an L3 whose
true stage is L2 must be COUNTED AS A NON-SURVIVOR, not deleted. A size
gate drops a detection, which would remove it from the numerator and the
denominator alike and quietly bias survival the other way. The fix belongs
in the survivor mapping, as a size-aware L2/L3 boundary, and it cannot be
set without ground truth: reassigning every sub-44 px L3 moves per-plate
survival by up to 42 points, and the worst-affected plates are the
unirradiated controls, which would reshape every dose-response curve.
Label the animals in label_worklist.csv (464 animals stratified across
34-54 px) and set the boundary from that. Until then, treat the survival
percentage as biased HIGH and prefer the body-size distribution, which
uses no class labels and is unaffected by this.
